what: Two-dimensional embeddings of the 220 operator rows of the final checkpoint's selection head, coloured by the paper's 7-way vocabulary partition. (a) PCA of the head output projection $W_{head}$ (220x1152), all rows; (b) UMAP of the same matrix; (c) PCA recomputed on the 59 rows added after the legacy base only, which is the only zoom in which the added operators are visible.
one_line_reading: The head's geometry does NOT carry the 7-way curriculum split: silhouette is negative (-0.094 over all 220 rows, -0.083 over the added 59). What it does carry is a legacy/added boundary -- 156/161 base rows (0.969) have their nearest neighbour inside the base block while the extension, curriculum, family and routing blocks score 0.000 each. Among the added rows the 1-NN purity is 0.407 against a chance level of 0.197, so there is real but coarse structure, not generation-aligned clusters.

method: weights read straight out of the checkpoint on CPU (no forward pass); PCA by SVD on column-centred rows; UMAP n_neighbors=15, min_dist=0.15, random_state=20260930; separability by leave-one-out 1-NN purity (cosine) and by the mean silhouette computed directly from the distance matrix.
caveats: NEGATIVE RESULT, registered deliberately: the naive claim 'the 7-way vocabulary partition is written into the head weights' is FALSE at this scale. The figure and this record state the measured alternative instead.
PC1+PC2 explain only 25% of the variance of $W_{head}$; a 2-D view is a weak summary and the negative silhouette is measured in the full 1152-d space, not in the projection.

The brief's index ranges are used verbatim. Index 178 ('bh_ineq_tail_other') is the one row that does not sit with its own bh_* family: it falls inside the 178..184 'construction curriculum' block because g24_* starts at 179.
Segment labels are the English forms used throughout the paper (base, deep-chain extension, construction curriculum, deep-chain family, substitution and evaluation, routing, expansion).
UMAP coordinates depend on the seed and on n_neighbors; panel (a) PCA is deterministic and is the one to quote quantitatively.

Base-block names for 0..153 come from V32REGISTRY insertion order, verified against the documented anchors (6=math_solve_linear_system, 7=math_simplify_expr, 8=math_expand_expr, 15=math_evaluate_expr, 95=mini_kernel_arith), because v32_op_index_map() returns an empty map without its data-loading build step.
